off.topRootCause: The recent Kafka broker patch caused the group coordinator to move, triggering repeated rebalances of the notif-worker consumer group. During rebalance, consumers paused, causing the otp.events topic lag to grow to ~84k messages, resulting in OTP dispatch timeouts.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the Kafka rebalance‑induced consumer lag, matching the ground truth.

on.topRootCause: The restart of kafka-1 as group coordinator forced an eager rebalance, triggering generation churn.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the rebalance‑storm caused by the broker restart, matching the ground‑truth cause.

rows.title: ledger-svc nightly reconciliation failing with DB errors

off.topTitle: Invalid DB credentials after secret rotation
off.topRootCause: Vault rotated the dynamic database credentials for ledger‑svc, but the service was not updated with the new password, leading to authentication failures and HikariPool initialization errors.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the secret rotation causing authentication failures, matching the ground truth mechanism.

on.topRootCause: Running ledger-svc pods have not picked up the newly rotated credentials and are using an expired lease.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the rotated secret causing stale credentials, matching the ground‑truth TLS secret expiry cause.

rows.title: Payout API errors after config change

off.topTitle: Bad config value for PAYOUT_BATCH_SIZE
off.topRootCause: The ConfigMap change introduced a non‑numeric value ('5k') for PAYOUT_BATCH_SIZE, and the code expects an integer, causing a ValueError and 500 responses for every payout request.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 exactly matches the ground truth bad-config-push cause.

on.topRootCause: The PAYOUT_BATCH_SIZE configuration was set to '5k', which is not a valid integer, causing a ValueError during application startup.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the bad configuration push causing the failure, matching the ground truth, whereas hypothesis #2 is vague.

rows.title: Festive sale day 1 — payments-api DB pool timeouts

off.topTitle: DB connection‑pool exhaustion under traffic spike
off.topRootCause: The sudden 4.5× traffic increase exhausts the SQLAlchemy connection pool (size 20 + overflow 10). New requests block waiting for a connection, causing timeouts and high request latency.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 blames the DB pool exhaustion as the primary cause, whereas the ground truth identifies a Redis eviction storm as the root cause.

on.topRootCause: High volume of requests failing to find cached configuration data due to mass key eviction.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the Redis eviction storm, matching the ground truth, whereas hypothesis #2 describes the downstream DB pool exhaustion, a symptom rather than the root cause.

rows.title: UPI collect requests expiring

off.topTitle: NPCI client pool saturation causing downstream bank timeouts (ICICI)
off.topRootCause: The npci-client connection pool reached near‑capacity, preventing timely requests to the ICICI bank endpoint. As a result, RespPay responses were not received within the 300 s window, leading to high collect expiries.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the NPCI client pool saturation leading to bank timeouts, which matches the ground‑truth cause.

on.topRootCause: ICICI bank degradation causing npci-client pool saturation
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 matches the ground‑truth cause (ICICI bank degradation leading to NPCI client pool saturation), while #2 is a broader NPCI timeout and #3 is unrelated.

rows.title: Merchant API 401 storm just after midnight

off.topTitle: JWT signing key rotation caused stale JWKS cache
off.topRootCause: The Vault rotation created a new version of the JWT signing key (kid=paynest-2026-10) but auth‑svc’s JWKS cache still held the old key (paynest-2026-09) for ~24h, causing token signature verification failures and 401 spikes.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 describes the same secret rotation and stale cache issue as the ground truth, matching the tls-secret-expiry family.

on.topTitle: Stale JWKS Cache after Key Rotation
on.topRootCause: The service is serving a stale JWKS from memory that does not contain the new key ID after a Vault rotation.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the stale JWKS cache after key rotation, matching the ground‑truth tls‑secret‑expiry cause.

rows.title: ledger-svc slow writes after parallel settlement rollout

off.topTitle: DB connection pool exhaustion after scaling change
off.topRootCause: The deployment raised Hikari maximumPoolSize to 80 and increased replicas, but PostgreSQL max_connections remained at 600. With 10 replicas each opening up to 80 connections, the total demand (~800) exceeds the DB limit, leading to pool timeouts and high write latency.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 exactly matches the ground truth description of DB pool exhaustion due to exceeding PostgreSQL max_connections.

on.topRootCause: Deployment of commit ec737ed increased Hikari maximumPoolSize and replicas, causing total connection demand to exceed the database max_connections limit.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the over‑provisioned Hikari pool exceeding the DB max_connections, matching the ground‑truth cause.

rows.title: Push notifications delayed after topic change

off.topTitle: Kafka consumer lag after partition increase
off.topRootCause: Increasing payment.events partitions caused a consumer group rebalance; notif‑worker instances failed to claim new partitions and fell behind, building up >200k messages of lag and delaying push notifications.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the rebalance‑induced consumer lag as the root cause, matching the ground truth.

on.topRootCause: Partition count increase triggered rebalance loop and CommitFailedException.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 matches the ground truth by pinpointing the partition count increase that triggered a rebalance loop and commit failures, which is the same mechanism causing the lag.

rows.title: payments-api 429 surge during festive traffic

off.topTitle: Rate‑limit misconfiguration causing per‑merchant throttling
off.topRootCause: The recent config push increased ratelimit.max_rps but did not propagate correctly to all pods or was applied with an unintended lower effective limit, causing merchants to hit the 50 rps ceiling.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 matches the ground‑truth cause (a config push typo setting a low ratelimit), whereas the others describe traffic spikes or downstream throttling, not the mis‑configured feature flag.

on.topRootCause: Recent commit 538abee introduced a typo setting ratelimit.max_rps to 50 instead of the expected value.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the typo in the config push that caused the throttling, matching the ground truth.

rows.title: upi-gateway long GC pauses and latency

off.topTitle: Logging library upgrade caused allocation surge
off.topRootCause: The new logging library version emits larger log objects and increased GC pressure, filling the heap and saturating the NPCI client executor queue, leading to GC pauses and request timeouts.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 blames a logging library allocation surge, whereas the ground truth attributes the issue to an NPCI bank timeout.

on.topRootCause: External bank degradation at NPCI causing thread pool saturation.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the NPCI/bank timeout cause, matching the ground truth, whereas #2 and #3 describe unrelated symptoms.

rows.title: VPA resolution slow on Dussehra evening

off.topTitle: Redis memory exhaustion causing eviction storm
off.topRootCause: The new deployment caches full VPA profiles (≈38 KB each), rapidly filling the 16 GB Redis instance. Near‑full memory triggers evictions and output‑buffer limits, leading to high cache‑miss rates and fallback to DB reads.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 matches the ground‑truth cause by describing Redis memory exhaustion and eviction storm, unlike the other hypotheses.

on.topRootCause: Deployment d007710 increased cache object size to ~38KB, reducing Redis capacity and causing memory exhaustion.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the Redis eviction storm caused by large VPA profile caching, matching the ground truth.

rows.title: Partner webhook deliveries failing

off.topTitle: TLS certificate expired on webhook endpoint
off.topRootCause: The TLS certificate for api.paynest.in expired (or is not yet valid) and cert‑manager could not complete a renewal due to an ACME 403 authorization error.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the TLS certificate expiration and renewal failure, matching the ground truth cause.

on.topRootCause: The certificate for api.paynest.in has expired and cert-manager is failing the DNS-01 challenge due to insufficient IAM permissions in Route53.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the TLS certificate expiry and DNS‑01 challenge failure, matching the ground truth.

rows.title: payments-api 5xx after festive HPA change

off.topTitle: DB connection pool exhaustion after HPA scale‑out
off.topRootCause: Increasing the number of pods caused each pod to open new DB connections, exceeding the PostgreSQL max_connections and pgbouncer max_client_conn limits, resulting in connection refusals and 5xx errors.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the DB connection pool exhaustion caused by HPA scaling, matching the ground truth.

on.topRootCause: Increased HPA maxReplicas caused total demand for database connections to exceed configured limits of pgbouncer and postgres.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the same DB pool exhaustion mechanism as the ground truth.

rows.title: Debit SMS not received — complaints spike

off.topTitle: Kafka consumer lag after poll interval breach
off.topRootCause: Increasing max.poll.records to 5000 caused the consumer to spend >300 s processing a batch (SMS provider call took ~2.2 s per batch), exceeding max.poll.interval.ms. The consumer was kicked out of the group, triggering a rebalance and leaving a backlog of ~300k messages, which reduced the SMS send rate.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the max.poll.records increase causing poll interval breach and consumer lag, matching the ground truth.

on.topRootCause: Increasing max.poll.records to 5000 while SMS calls remain synchronous causes processing time to exceed max.poll.interval.ms.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the same poll‑interval timeout mechanism as the ground truth, just phrased as a sync processing timeout.

rows.title: Refunds failing with ledger-svc 404s

off.topTitle: Feature‑flag rollout points to missing service version
off.topRootCause: The `refund_via_ledger_v2` flag was enabled, causing payments‑api to call `/v2/refunds` on ledger‑svc, but the Ledger service is still running only v1 (no `/v2/refunds` route). The upstream 404 is translated to 502 by the API gateway, inflating the refund failure rate.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the bad feature‑flag push causing calls to a missing v2 endpoint, matching the ground‑truth cause.

on.topRootCause: The refund_via_ledger_v2 flag enabled traffic to a path that does not exist on the target ledger-svc.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 matches the ground truth by identifying the same feature‑flag misconfiguration that caused traffic to hit a non‑existent endpoint.

rows.title: UPI success rate collapse across ALL banks

off.topTitle: TLS secret expiry for NPCI communication
off.topRootCause: The TLS certificate used by upi-gateway to authenticate to NPCI expired or was replaced without updating the secret in the cluster, causing handshake failures across all payer banks.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the TLS certificate expiration causing the failure, matching the ground truth.

on.topRootCause: The mTLS client certificate used for communication with NPCI has expired.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly identifies the mTLS client certificate expiry, matching the ground truth.

rows.title: payments-api readiness flapping overnight

off.topTitle: DB connection pool exhaustion caused by settlement‑report threads
off.topRootCause: The new settlement‑report background workers (8 threads per pod) are using the same SQLAlchemy request pool as the API handlers, exceeding the configured pool size (20) and overflow (10), leading to timeouts and readiness failures.
off.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 describes the same DB pool exhaustion mechanism as the ground truth.

on.topTitle: Settlement-report background threads exhausting DB pool
on.topRootCause: Background thread pool sharing the main request database connection pool.
on.judgeReason: Hypothesis #1 correctly describes the DB pool exhaustion described in the ground truth, while the others do not.
